messages:
morgan: FYI a Dedicated customer is hitting 404s when calling chat endpoints using the TypeScript SDK v0.22.0. They say it started after a node module update.
morgan: Repro steps they gave:
```js
import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference-js';
const c = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
await c.chat.create({ model: 'gpt-redwood-1', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hi' }], session: 's-123' });
// => 404 /v1/chat.create
```

sara: thanks — can you paste the error body and the full request/response from the Dedicated proxy? pinging jamal for any recent route renames. :eyes:

morgan: error body is short, 404 + "route not found". Customer used our hosted base url but points to their Dedicated region (eu-1). I asked for proxy logs, attaching excerpt:
```
proxy -> api: POST /v1/chat.create 404
upstream: 404 {"error":"route not found","path":"/v1/chat.create"}
```

jamal: quick note: we shipped an API route rename last month to standardize on REST-y names. The canonical route is now POST /v1/chat/create (underscore/dot variants deprecated). SDK v0.22.0 still emits the older dotted routes in the client wrapper. Looks like Dedicated customers with stricter routing are getting 404s.

morgan: ah ok. Is this a customer config mismatch or a bug in the SDK vs Dedicated control plane?

jamal: root cause is the SDK packaging: the generated client code shipped with old route strings. Hosted API supports both for backward compat, but Dedicated control planes default to strict routing to reduce noise. We'll need an SDK patch that updates the path strings and a short-lived compatibility shim on Dedicated.

sara: for the customer workaround: they can either call the raw REST endpoint or specify a custom path in the client until we publish a fix. Example raw call:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://eu-1.dedicated.redwood.ai/v1/chat/create" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-redwood-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"conversationId":"s-123"}'
```
(also note param rename: session -> conversationId in the newer API)

morgan: customer confirmed they can call the /v1/chat/create path directly and it works. They want an ETA on an SDK release (they rely on the SDK in CI).

jamal: I'll open a patch now. Plan: bump client generator and release @redwood/inference-js v0.22.1 with updated paths and param names (backwards-compatible overloads). If QA looks good we can cut a release in ~3 hours. I'll attach PR.

jamal: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-js/pull/412 — updates route table, adds tests for Dedicated proxy, adds deprecation warning when calling old dotted routes.

oss-bot: CI passed on main (unit + e2e) — build #5841

deploy-bot: released @redwood/inference-js v0.22.1 to npm and tagged canary. Changelog: fix(route): use /v1/chat/create and accept conversationId (fixes Dedicated 404s)

morgan: pushing the customer the patched package and a short note about the param rename and the temporary workaround. They asked if we can enable compat routing on their Dedicated cluster while they upgrade.

jamal: ops can flip compat-mode for that cluster for 48h. @ops-team please enable legacy-route-alias on eu-1.dedicated for customer-acme until midnight UTC.

sara: ops confirmed via DM they enabled the alias. Customer upgraded to v0.22.1 and verified SDK calls work again. They also ran a quick regression test against chat flows.

morgan: customer happy and unblocked. closing the escalation. Thanks everyone. :tada:

jamal: follow-up action items: 1) add a note to the SDK release notes and support KB about route renames, 2) add a canary test for Dedicated strict routes in our e2e matrix, 3) scan other SDK languages for same bug.

sara: filed KB: https://redwood.company/kb/sdk-route-compat and incident ticket #INC-2020 with postmortem stub.

morgan: closing thread. final timestamps and links saved in the support ticket.
